name: iBMS alarms and trends
label: iBMS alarm
description: Replays recorded alarm and trend events from the incident timelines; no building system is connected. In production it would read alarm points bound by Brick class, so one pill runs at any site whose points are tagged. An authenticated endpoint (POST /api/ingest) accepts this system's own payload today and maps it to evidence keys; nothing it posts can confirm an item a gate needs.

name: Leak detection cables
system: Leak detection panel (brick:Leak_Alarm), reported through the iBMS
label: Leak detector
description: In the demo, detector alarms such as LD-23-04 and LD-DH2-01 arrive as recorded iBMS events. In production the panel's points would be read through the same iBMS adapter; a detector can raise an incident, never confirm where the water is. An authenticated endpoint (POST /api/ingest) accepts this system's own payload today and maps it to evidence keys; nothing it posts can confirm an item a gate needs.

name: CMMS work orders
label: CMMS work order
description: Replays recorded work orders. A work order that links the isolation diagram is accepted as the shut-off map being in hand: a document on file, not a sensor reading. In production, work orders would be matched to assets by CMMS asset code. The same payload can arrive live at POST /api/ingest; an ingested work order reports the map as unconfirmed, because the person who read it is the one who confirms it.

name: Tenant hotline
system: Tenant hotline, logged by the Asset Operations Manager
label: Tenant call
description: Recorded tenant calls. A named Asset Operations Manager logs each call and confirms what the caller reports; the caller never confirms anything. Calls carry tenant data and are masked for roles not cleared for it.

name: Tenant experience desk
label: Tenant experience
description: Recorded entries by the Tenant Experience Manager, such as reaching the account manager and setting the next tenant update. In production these would come from the tenant experience team's own log.

name: Technician field app
label: Technician
description: Recorded observations, photos and actions entered by a named technician on site. In production this would be the field app the technician already uses; each entry carries who made it and when.

name: Technical Services duty log
label: Technical Services
description: Recorded dispatches and findings by the named Technical Services Lead, such as calling the duty LEW or confirming the failed component.

name: Critical facilities desk
label: Critical facilities
description: Recorded entries by the named Critical Facilities Manager at the data centre: SLA terms on file, client impact and the co-signature for return to service.

name: LEW sign-off
label: LEW sign-off
description: Recorded inspections and written sign-offs by the named duty LEW. The sign-off and insulation-resistance items that the re-energise gate (TS-07) needs can be confirmed only by the duty LEW; no feed can.

name: Contractor reports
label: Contractor
description: Proposed for a pilot: contractor job reports attached to the work order. Not built; in the demo, contractor work is reported by Technical Services.

name: DCIM
label: DCIM
description: Proposed for a pilot: hall temperatures and N+1 cooling state from the data centre's DCIM. Not built; in the demo, data-hall alarms arrive as recorded iBMS events.

name: LLM drafting chain
system: CodeBuddy SDK, then TokenHub hy4-preview (ap-singapore), then OpenAI
label: LLM draft
description: Drafts rules from interview and note transcripts, and tenant messages. Tries each provider that has credentials, in order, and falls back to a labelled recorded draft. Output is always a draft for a named person to check.

name: Jev evidence suggestions
label: Jev suggestion
description: Suggests which evidence items look likely from the incident so far. A suggestion is never evidence: a person in an allowed role must confirm it before a gate reads it.

name: Tencent Cloud ADP agent
label: ADP agent
description: Asks an agent on Tencent Cloud ADP, the enterprise platform a pill would be published to, a question in plain language. The adapter posts to the documented chat endpoint with an AppKey and no request signing, which a live probe confirmed is the whole credential; this account has no AppKey yet, so Keystone does not call it. An answer would be drafting help for a person, never a gate decision.

name: Tencent Cloud ASR
label: Tencent ASR
description: Speech to text processed in Singapore for frontline voice notes. The adapter is typed and tested but has not been verified against the live service, so Keystone does not use it.

name: OpenAI transcription
label: OpenAI transcription
description: Optional speech to text for voice notes. Off unless explicitly enabled, because the audio leaves Singapore. The audio is never stored.

name: Browser speech recognition
system: Web Speech API in the viewer's browser
label: Browser speech
description: The no-key baseline for voice notes. Depends on your browser: in most browsers the audio is processed by the browser vendor's service. Typing a note always works.

name: Skill package export
system: Zip download (SKILL.md, rules, evidence, provenance, evals, changelog)
label: Skill package
description: Downloads the approved version of a pill as a skill folder, built in your browser from the governance record. Tested to load back through the pill loader with the same eval results.

name: Incident decision record
label: Decision record
description: One incident's pills and versions, gates and their evidence, named-human decisions and audit trail, masked for your role. Print it or download it as JSON.

name: Audit log export
label: Audit log
description: Downloads the append-only audit log from the audit drawer, as CSV for a spreadsheet or JSON for another system.
